figs/9756de9d63476a79.jpg: **At P60, mtDSB raises ISR/UPR genes in mature oligodendrocytes far more than in other glia (legacy group-level analysis).** Each panel is one cell type (telencephalon astrocytes, microglia, olfactory astrocytes, OPCs, mature OLs); each bar is one ISR/UPR gene, showing its pseudobulk pyDESeq2 log2 fold change mtDSB vs control at P60 (3 vs 3 mice, all mtDSB mice pooled regardless of response). Red bars have raw p < 0.1 (not adjusted); grey bars do not; only genes with mean CPM > 30 are shown, and the text at right gives fold change and mean CPM. Mature OLs stand out, led by Trib3 (log2FC about 5.1, 34.2x), Atf5 (3.0x) and Gadd45a (2.4x), while the other glia shift by 1.5x or less. This legacy figure underpins the old "P60 strong" claim, which was later traced to two responders at P60 versus one at P21.
figs/f0e1427d21648474.jpg: **At P21 the same legacy ISR/UPR comparison looks weak, because only one of the three P21 mtDSB mice responds.** The layout matches the P60 version: each panel is a glial cell type and each bar is the pseudobulk pyDESeq2 log2FC mtDSB vs control at P21 for one ISR/UPR gene (3 vs 3 mice), with red marking raw p < 0.1 and mean CPM > 30 required. Mature OLs again lead with Trib3 (log2FC about 3.9, 14.8x) and Atf5 (2.0x), but the only bars reaching p < 0.1 are Ero1l and Ero1lb. The other glia stay near zero. Read beside the P60 panel, this was once taken as "P21 modest, P60 strong"; the later explanation is that P21 has one responder and P60 has two, so dilution differs between ages.
figs/63fa2339cef617d3.jpg: **Region-specific OL treatment effects at P60 are few, and all are neuropeptide or neuronal transcripts.** Each grey point is one gene in one region: x is the mtDSB-vs-control log2FC in OLs from the rest of the section and y is the log2FC in OLs from that region (section-level pseudobulk, 3 vs 3 mice); the dashed diagonal marks equal effects. Purple points have a significant region-minus-rest difference (z-test, BH padj < 0.05); there are 4. The four are Pmch in cortex, fibre tracts and hypothalamus, and Ntsr1 in hypothalamus. These are neuronal transcripts picked up by OLs (spill-over), not OL biology, so the group-level analysis shows no genuine region-specific OL response at P60.
figs/687ac19bfb14a9a2.jpg: **Most significant mtDSB-vs-control genes sit in NSCs and neurons, not in oligodendrocytes.** Each block is one cell type, with rows for regions (plus a whole-section "All regions" row) and columns for P21 and P60. Each cell gives the number of significant genes from a section-level pseudobulk pyDESeq2 Wald test (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5, baseMean >= 20; 3 vs 3 sections); a dash means the stratum could not be tested, and colour is capped at 45. NSCs at P60 dominate (671 ventricular, 654 whole-section; caused by ventricle coverage and section plane), then neurons in striatum (108 at P60) and hypothalamus (44/47). Oligodendrocytes have few hits (8 whole-section at P60; 13 in hypothalamus at P21, mostly neuropeptide spill-over).
figs/8c5f1748b01ebb08.jpg: **At group level, whole-section OL DE at P60 finds only 8 significant genes; the large ISR fold changes do not reach significance.** Each point is one gene in the whole-section OL pseudobulk (pyDESeq2, 3 mtDSB vs 3 control sections at P60); x is log2FC mtDSB vs control and y is -log10 padj, with dashed lines at |log2FC| = 0.5 and padj = 0.05. Red (6 up) and blue (2 down) mark significant genes. The strongest hits are the neuropeptides Pmch and Hcrt (down) and neuronal Gabra2 and Trh (up), all spill-over; Gfap, Gpnmb, Rec8 and Atf5 also pass. Trib3 (log2FC about 4), Cst7, Gdf15, Cdkn1a and Cd40 have large effects but stay near padj 1, because 3 of the 6 mtDSB mice do not respond and dilute them. Mt2 (labelled, grey) clears padj but falls just under the 0.5 log2FC cut-off.
figs/8ca44dc3b131319a.jpg: **OL stress and mitokine genes rise in nearly every region at both ages, even where they are not significant.** Rows are prespecified stress / mitokine / immune genes and columns are region x age strata for oligodendrocytes. Colour is the pyDESeq2 log2FC mtDSB vs control from section-level pseudobulks (3 vs 3; capped at ±3), shown unmasked whatever the padj; blank cells are genes not tested in that stratum. Trib3, Gdf15, Cdkn1a, Cd40, Cst7 and Serpina3n are red almost everywhere, and the strongest are in thalamus and fibre tracts at P60. Hcrt and Pmch flip sign between regions and ages, the pattern expected for neuropeptide spill-over rather than OL biology.
figs/d9eaecb5340fbaed.jpg: **Most NSC hits are a coordinated loss of NSC/ependymal genes at P60, which reflects section plane.** Rows are the top significant neural-stem-cell genes and columns are the ventricular-system and whole-section strata at P21 and P60. Colour is the log2FC mtDSB vs control from section-level pseudobulk pyDESeq2; cells with padj >= 0.05 are blank. At P60 every gene (Col23a1, Gpr50, Crym, Slit2, Slc16a2 and others) is strongly down in mtDSB, while P21 shows only small effects. The run notes attribute this to how much ventricle each section captured (cutting plane), not to mtDSB.
figs/ea5c83c867ec2bca.jpg: **Microglia carry a whole-section activation signal (Cst7, Cd74, Gpnmb, Serpina3n) in mtDSB brains, strongest at P60.** The layout matches the OL panel: rows are prespecified stress / mitokine / immune genes, columns are region x age strata, and colour is the unmasked pyDESeq2 log2FC mtDSB vs control in microglial pseudobulks (3 vs 3; capped at ±3), with blank cells untested. Cst7, Cd74 and Gpnmb are deep red in most regions, and thalamus and fibre tracts at P60 are the most consistent. At group level these changes are not significant (e.g. Cd74 and Cst7 padj 0.15 whole-section at P60). Hcrt and Pmch again flip sign, consistent with spill-over.
figs/2be208b6a40e3db7.jpg: **No OL stress gene changes its treatment effect between ages; the top age x condition genes in whole-section OLs are neuropeptide and neuronal transcripts.** Each row is one of the 20 genes with the smallest interaction p-value in the whole-section OL pseudobulk model (~ age + condition + age:condition; sections as replicates, 3 per age x condition). Orange and blue dots give the mtDSB-vs-control log2FC at P21 and P60, joined by a grey line; an asterisk marks interaction padj < 0.05. Only Hcrt, Gabra2 and C1ql1 are significant, and Hcrt and Pmch swing from up at P21 to down at P60, which is typical of spill-over from hypothalamic neurons. Trib3, Atf5, Gdf15 and Cdkn1a do not appear among the top interaction genes.
figs/450e04e365565583.jpg: **Microglial treatment effects mostly agree between P21 and P60, with no consistent age-dependent genes.** Each panel is one region (plus All regions) and each point is one gene: x is the mtDSB-vs-control log2FC in microglial pseudobulk at P21 and y is the same at P60 (3 vs 3 sections per age); the dashed line is y = x. Colour shows where the gene is significant (padj < 0.05: P21 only orange, P60 only blue, both purple, neither grey); open black rings mark a significant P60-minus-P21 difference (z-test on the two fold changes). Activation genes (Cst7, Cd74, Gpnmb, Serpina3n) sit above zero at both ages, highest in thalamus. The few ringed genes are neuronal (e.g. Slc17a6, Adcyap1 in striatum; Pdyn, Nptx2 in hypothalamus), so they look like spill-over. Point counts in the legend refer to the first panel only.
figs/b768073994b7d7a1.jpg: **OL stress genes move the same way at both ages; age-dependent hits are neuropeptides.** Each panel is one region (plus All regions) and each point is one gene: x is the mtDSB-vs-control log2FC in OL pseudobulk at P21 and y the same at P60 (3 vs 3 sections per age); the dashed line is y = x. Colours mark per-age significance (padj < 0.05: P21 only orange, P60 only blue, both purple, neither grey) and black rings mark a significant P60-minus-P21 difference (z-test). Trib3, Cst7, Cd40, Gdf15 and Cdkn1a lie in the upper-right quadrant near the diagonal in most regions, so the response is present at both ages. The ringed genes are Hcrt and Pmch (hypothalamus, thalamus, whole section), plus Cd74 in thalamus, a microglial gene. Legend counts apply to the first panel only.
figs/53785d4702b6224f.jpg: **A prespecified ISR gene set splits the six mtDSB mice into three clear responders and three that look like controls.** (A) Each point is one mouse (one section): the summed CPM of 10 canonical ATF4 / mitochondrial ISR genes in its whole-section oligodendrocyte pseudobulk. Blue = control, filled orange = responder, open orange = non-responder; the dashed line is the responder threshold, 1.2x the highest control. RB4405, RB4627 and RB4401 (about 3,500-4,000 CPM) stand well above every control (about 2,000-2,600), while RB4403, RB4630 and RB4653 fall inside the control range. (B) Per-gene log2FC of each mouse against the six-control mean; Atf5, Ddit3, Trib3, Gdf15, Sesn2 and Eif4ebp1 rise only in the three responders, and Psat1 falls in two of them.
figs/dc5731743c65029a.jpg: **Three readouts built from different inputs rank the same three mice on top.** Each row is one mouse (section) and the panels are three section-level readouts: (A) the prespecified ISR gene-set CPM in oligodendrocytes; (B) the mean held-out p(mtDSB) of the mouse's OLs from a single-cell classifier trained leave-one-section-out on the other 11 sections; (C) the share of OLs in the DA-oligodendrocyte cluster (log scale). Blue = control, filled orange = responder, open orange = non-responder. RB4405, RB4627 and RB4401 lead on all three. Non-responders sit at or below controls, lowest on the classifier (0.28-0.37). The DA cluster holds 21-65% of OLs in responders and about 2% or less elsewhere. The readouts share OL expression, so they are not fully independent.
figs/35b934ad097aed4f.jpg: **Sex, white-matter content and section size do not explain which mtDSB mice respond.** Each row is one mouse (section), coloured by group (blue control, filled orange responder, open orange non-responder). (A) Whole-section Xist CPM against the recorded sex (M/F in the row label); every female is about 400 CPM and every male near 0, so labels match and both responders and non-responders include each sex. (B) Percentage of cells in fibre tracts: responders 8.8-10.8% overlap the others (5.8-9.5%). (C) Cells per section: all about 70,000-89,000 except non-responder RB4403 at about 135,000, a likely segmentation outlier.
figs/b6a72b27f94fae58.jpg: **Age is easy to predict, condition is not; OL classifiers transferred between age cohorts pick out the responders.** (A) Leave-one-section-out AUC of pseudobulk logistic regressions per cell type (rows) and task (columns: age, pooled condition, condition within each age, and cross-cohort transfer 21->60 and 60->21); colour clipped at 0.5, asterisks mark permutation p (* <= 0.05, ** <= 0.01). Age reaches 0.78-1.00 in most cell types, while pooled condition stays at 0.11-0.58 with no stars (OLs 0.44). Within-age tasks are 3 vs 3 and cannot reach p < 0.05. (B) Each point is one mouse: the mean held-out p(mtDSB) of its OLs from single-cell models, either pooled LOSO or trained on one age cohort and tested on the other. Responders (labelled filled orange) top every column: RB4627 is the top P21 mouse when trained on P60, and RB4405 and RB4401 top P60 when trained on P21. Non-responders (open) sit with controls.
figs/29615c6f8f49b25b.jpg: **In responders every region is shifted, most strongly fibre tracts and thalamus.** Rows are brain regions (original read-based region map) and columns are the 12 mice, ordered controls, non-responders, responders. Each cell gives a section x region readout divided by the mean of the six controls in that region: (A) ISR gene-set score, (B) fraction of OLs with classifier p > 0.8, (C) share of OLs in the DA cluster (absolute share, 0-0.8). White cells are regions with fewer than 50 OLs, such as vasculature in several mice and pallidum in RB4405. Only the three responders (right) are dark across all regions, and RB4405 is the most severe. Fibre tracts and thalamus rank highest on average. Later analyses on a disease-free region map added pallidum to this top group.
figs/2ab07b302cb3045a.jpg: **In responders a quarter to two-fifths of all OLs score above the control range, spread across the whole section.** Each map is one coronal section (top row P21, bottom row P60; controls left, mtDSB right). Each dot is one oligodendrocyte: grey OLs score at or below the 90th percentile of pooled control OLs on the held-out single-cell classifier p(mtDSB) (0.979), and orange OLs score above it; the light grey background is all other cells. The header gives each mouse's group and its share of "high" OLs. Responders reach 24-40% (RB4627, RB4401, RB4405) against 5-16% in controls and 4-6% in non-responders, and the high OLs are densest in thalamus and white matter but present everywhere.
figs/41145be056370b08.jpg: **A per-cell ISR score marks a dense, brain-wide band of stressed OLs only in the three responders.** (A) Distribution per mouse of each OL's ISR score (10 prespecified genes, smoothed over its 15 nearest OLs), expressed as a percentile of control OLs on the same slide; the mouse mean is in brackets and the dashed line marks the 90th percentile. Controls (blue) and non-responders (dashed orange) are roughly flat, while responders (filled orange) pile up at the top. (B) Maps of every OL coloured by that percentile (blue below, red above the control median; dorsal up, midline right), with the share above the control 90th percentile in each header. Responders reach 31-55%, compared with 7-13% for controls and 8-14% for non-responders, and the signal is strongest in thalamus and white matter. The 15-OL smoothing is for display and makes the maps look more spatially coherent than single cells are.
figs/9af6e7f01302bc15.jpg: **On the classifier score, responder OLs sit high across the section while non-responder OLs sit below controls.** (A) Per-mouse distribution of each OL's held-out classifier p(mtDSB), expressed as a percentile of pooled control OLs; the dashed line marks the 90th percentile. Responders (filled orange) are skewed to the top and non-responders (dashed) to the bottom. (B) Every OL on its section map (top row P21, bottom row P60), coloured from blue (below the control median) to red (above), with the mouse median in each header. Medians are 65-85 in responders, 38-63 in controls and 23-35 in non-responders; RB4403 is blue almost everywhere. Classifier probabilities are poorly calibrated, so they are shown as control percentiles.
figs/411c8decd13ae634.jpg: **Outside OLs, single-cell classifiers predict age perfectly but not condition; only cross-cohort transfer gives weak hints.** Rows are 12 cell types and columns are prediction tasks: age, pooled condition, condition within P21 or P60, and cross-cohort transfer (train on P21 and test on P60, or the reverse). Each cell is the leave-one-section-out AUC of a single-cell logistic regression whose cell predictions are averaged to one value per section (colour clipped at 0.5; blank = not computed). Age reaches AUC 1.0 in 10 of 12 types, while pooled condition is 0.07-0.50. Transfer AUCs of 0.67-1.0 appear in astrocytes, endothelium, microglia and OLs (e.g. endothelial 60->21 = 1.00), but these rest on 3 vs 3 sections and have no permutation test.
figs/226cf04af815553a.jpg: **In responders the up-driver programme is raised and myelin genes are lowered in every region, most in thalamus and fibre tracts.** Rows are brain regions (original map) and each point is one mouse: blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder. (D) Mean log2FC of the 34 up-driver genes in that region's OL pseudobulk relative to the control mean of the same region; (E) the same for the 9 down-regulated myelin / mature-OL genes. Responders are separated from all other mice in every region, with group means highest in thalamus (about 1.6) and fibre tracts. One responder is higher in ventricular system (about 2.2) and fibre tracts (about 2.0) than in its own thalamus. Pallidum has only two responder points because the original map absorbed responder pallidum into fibre tracts. Panels are lettered D/E although the figure stands alone.
figs/91d7cebc487ab2e8.jpg: **Inside responder sections, 34 genes rise and 9 myelin genes fall with an OL's stress score, while controls show no such link.** Each point is one gene. x is its mean within-section Pearson r with the OL classifier score (logit of held-out p(mtDSB)) across the six control sections, and y is the same across the three responder sections (159,301 OLs scored; correlation computed per section, so section-level confounds cancel). Orange and blue mark driver genes, defined before inspection as r > 0.1 in each responder and mean r < 0.1 in controls and non-responders (mirror rule for down genes); the dashed line is y = x. Trib3 (r about 0.29), Cdkn1a, Cd40, Serpina3n, Atf5 and Mt2 lead the up-drivers, and Cldn11, Mog, Mal and Cnp lead the down-drivers. Drivers are genes that co-vary with a score trained on condition labels.
figs/d2c5df214c826dd7.jpg: **The driver programme is present in all three responders and absent in every control and non-responder.** Rows are the 43 driver genes grouped into manually annotated programmes (ATF4 / ISR, mitochondrial and protein quality control, cell cycle / survival, immune / reactive, OL lineage, cytoskeleton, lipid, mature OL / myelin down, other). Columns are the 12 mice (controls, non-responders, responders). Colour is the whole-section OL pseudobulk log2FC of each mouse against the six-control mean (±3). Trib3, Cdkn1a, Cd40 and Serpina3n are strongly up in RB4627, RB4401 and RB4405 only, and the myelin genes (Cldn11, Mog, Mal) are down most in RB4405, the most severe responder.
figs/70e9f3e6de7326e1.jpg: **Two OL classifiers trained on disjoint sets of mice share their top stress and myelin genes far above chance.** Each point is one gene: x is its weight in an OL single-cell logistic regression trained only on the six P21 mice, and y its weight in one trained only on the six P60 mice. Orange marks genes in both models' top-50 positive weights (10 shared, 0.49 expected; hypergeometric p = 2.4e-11) and blue marks genes in both top-50 negative weights (4 shared, p = 0.0014); black rings mark glucocorticoid-response genes. Genome-wide the weights barely correlate (Spearman 0.035), but Trib3, Atf5, Mt2 and Bcl2l1 (stress) and Cldn11 and Opalin (myelin) replicate. Part of the overlap is shared section-level state rather than mtDSB: the glucocorticoid genes Plin4 and Zbtb16, and Il33, earlier flagged as a one-control confound.
figs/4d37193e41dc719a.jpg: **Astrocytes and microglia next to stressed OLs are more activated in responders; endothelium is not.** Top row: each point is one mouse, giving the within-section Pearson r between a glial cell's activation score and the mean ISR score of OLs within 50 um (both centred within section x region). Groups are control, non-responder and responder, and the exact permutation p (responders vs controls, 84 relabellings, floor 0.012) is in each title. Reactive astrocytes (p = 0.012) and microglial DAM (p = 0.048) couple more strongly in responders; homeostatic microglia (p = 0.131) and endothelial activation (p = 0.869) do not. Bottom row: the mean centred neighbour score (±SEM shading) per decile of local OL stress, for control (blue) and responder (orange) cells. The readout gene sets overlap genes that OLs themselves raise, so some coupling may be OL RNA picked up by neighbouring glia.
figs/de4236c05b9918de.jpg: **Stressed OLs come first and myelin loss follows: the share of stressed OLs that have also lost myelin genes rises with severity.** (A) For each mouse, stacked bars give the percentage of OLs that are ISR-high with normal myelin, ISR-high with low myelin, or ISR-normal with low myelin. ISR-high means above the 90th and myelin-low below the 10th percentile of same-slide, same-region control OLs, both smoothed over 15 neighbours; responders are ordered by severity. (B) Mean myelin percentile across ISR percentile bins, one line per mouse (blue controls, dashed non-responders, thick orange responders); myelin falls as ISR rises, most steeply in responders. (C) P(myelin-low given ISR-high) per mouse: RB4401 0.40, RB4627 0.73, RB4405 0.90, against 0.09-0.25 in controls (p = 0.012). This is a cross-section of animals of different severity, not a time course; non-responder RB4403 has a high myelin-low share, likely from over-segmentation.
figs/887ba0b5731201bf.jpg: **A microglia's own expression predicts how close it sits to a stressed OL, in responders only.** (A-C) Each point is one held-out mouse: the Pearson r between predicted and true distance to the nearest stressed OL (log distance adjusted for region, OL density and distance to any OL). Predictions come from ridge regression on the cell's own expression, with OL-enriched, driver and ISR genes removed (strict features). Columns: control models tested on controls (the null), responder models tested on held-out responders, and the responder model applied to controls and to non-responders (open). Microglia separate clearly (responders 0.135-0.196 vs controls 0.076-0.126, p = 0.012); astrocytes do so weakly (p = 0.024) and endothelium does not (p = 0.774). (D) The 20 largest microglial ridge weights (negative = closer to stressed OLs): Cd68, Cd83 and Trem2 (orange, activation / phagocytic) sit among neuronal genes (Scn4b, Hcn1, Pde10a; grey), which are likely neighbourhood spill-over.
figs/6bfc232285beff6e.jpg: **An induction check is the only design that reaches 80 % power with 5-6 mice per group.** Simulated power (one-sided, alpha 0.05; 600 simulations per point) against the number of mice per group, for four tests: Mann-Whitney on group means (grey), a variance test (blue), a count of mtDSB mice above the control maximum (orange), and the group mean after an ideal induction QC that drops non-responders (green). Panel A assumes 50 % of mtDSB mice respond, panel B 75 %; the dashed line marks 0.8 power. With half responding, the classic mean comparison stays below 0.7 even at 12 mice, variance and count need about 10, while the QC'd mean reaches 0.8 at 5. The zig-zag of the variance test at 4-5 mice is a small-sample artefact, not a real effect.
figs/88e46bf716e85ed7.jpg: **Responder OL stress does not increase towards the ventricles, meninges or vessels.** A-C: one dot per section (mouse; filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder) showing the rank correlation between each OL's smoothed ISR score and its log distance to the nearest ventricle, meningeal surface or endothelial cell, after centring within region; positive means more stress farther away. Responders vs controls by exact permutation give p = 0.10, 0.25 and 0.08, and responder correlations are, if anything, more positive (more stress away from the borders). D: mean OL stress percentile (relative to same-slide, same-region controls) by distance to the ventricle, mean ± SEM over mice; responders sit at roughly the 75th-80th control percentile at every distance, controls near 50, so there is no outside-in gradient.
figs/37250024deed31cd.jpg: **Neighbouring OLs share stress no more in responders than in controls: the response is diffuse, not focal.** Spatial correlogram: for each section (one line), the correlation between an OL's raw ISR score and the mean ISR of other OLs in a ring at the given distance band (0-25 to 200-400 um, log-spaced x axis), both centred within region. Blue thin lines = controls, thick orange = responders, dashed orange = non-responders. Responder lines lie within the control spread at every band (all r about 0.02-0.12; permutation p 0.08-0.89), so stressed OLs do not form patches; all correlations are small because the single-cell 10-gene score is noisy.
figs/2ab00c4a9a578956.jpg: **No repair response: immature OLs neither gather near stressed OLs nor are more abundant in responders.** One dot per section (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder). A: per-section correlation between an OL's smoothed ISR and the local fraction of immature OLs within 50 um (region-centred); responders are not higher (p = 0.98). B: fraction of all cells that are immature OLs per section (about 2.5-3.4 %), similar across groups. C-D: in pre-myelinating immature OL II cells, the correlation of the cell's proliferation (C) or newly-formed-OL (D) score with the mean ISR of OLs within 50 um; responders trend higher (both p = 0.07) but overlap the control range, a weak, non-significant hint.
figs/9c6fd206d5bed564.jpg: **Neurons next to stressed OLs show no consistent axon-injury response.** One dot per section (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder): correlation between each neuron's axon-injury gene score and the mean ISR of OLs within 50 um, centred within region, for four neuron classes (excitatory, GABAergic, medium spiny, and the generic 'Neurons' class). Responders vs controls by one-sided permutation: p = 0.63, 0.70, 0.83 and 0.04. The single nominal hit (generic 'Neurons', small r, 8 uncorrected tests including the ISR readout not shown here) is most likely chance; the neuronal ISR readouts are not plotted.
figs/0ca9d60534497a3e.jpg: **Three mtDSB mice respond with near certainty, two do not, and RB4630 remains an open, weak candidate.** A: each mouse's whole-section OL ISR, in control SDs above its slide's control mean (x), with its posterior probability of being a responder from a two-component Bayesian mixture; orange = mtDSB (filled = called responders, open = non-responders, shaded band), blue = controls, each scored as if unlabelled and left out of the reference. RB4627, RB4405 and RB4401 have P > 0.99, RB4630 P = 0.17, and no control exceeds 0.08. B: posterior of the fraction of mtDSB mice that respond (mean 0.52, 90 % CI 0.23-0.80), so six mice cannot pin down the rate. C: P(responder) for each mtDSB mouse (R = responder, NR = non-responder) under nine prior variants; the three responders stay at 0.99-1.00, while RB4630 ranges 0.01-0.34 except 0.67 under the 'shift up to 6 SD' prior. D: predicted P(responder) for a new mouse as a function of its ISR fold over its slide's control mean, with the six mtDSB mice as dots; P reaches 0.9 at 1.17x.
figs/41a824eb360c8f54.jpg: **Trbc1 and Ighm probes are off-target; the nine core T-cell probes are sparse.** Number of cells (log scale, all 12 sections) with at least one transcript of each lymphocyte probe; the label beside each bar gives the cell class holding the largest share of those cells. Ighm (about 68k cells) and Trbc1 (about 30k cells, 70 % excitatory neurons) light up far too many cells, mostly neurons, so they were excluded (grey). Core probes (blue: Cd3d/e/g, Cd247, Cd2, Cd8a/b1, Itk, Cxcr6) are each detected in roughly 300-2,000 cells.
figs/4a0062f282964dac.jpg: **Cells co-expressing T-cell genes are real: 242 calls against about 4 by chance, with a CD8 / Cxcr6 profile.** A: number of cells called T cells (at least 3 core transcripts from at least 2 core genes) in the observed data versus a null where each core gene is shuffled across cells within each section (mean of 20 shuffles, error bar), about 60x. B: mean transcripts per cell of T-cell genes in the 242 called cells (red) versus all other cells with at least one core transcript (grey). Called cells carry Cd8a/b1, Cxcr6, Ptprc, Lck, Lat and Il7r with some Gzma, but little Cd4; Trbc1 is high in them (about 2.3 per cell) even though it was not used for the call.
figs/864cc70157f81285.jpg: **T cells take the labels of their neighbours: none of the 242 is annotated as a lymphocyte.** Number of called T cells per label under three annotations: cell_class_updated (left), cell_type (middle) and the cytetype annotation of leiden_3 clusters (right). Most are labelled endothelial (133), astrocytes (44) or DA-oligodendrocytes (37); at finer level vascular leptomeningeal cells, mature oligodendrocytes V and vascular endothelial cells dominate, and in cytetype a 'stress-responsive oligodendrocyte' cluster holds the most (39). T cells are too rare to form their own cluster, so they are absorbed into whatever surrounds them (vessels, meninges, OL-rich tissue).
figs/da998ea7ac6eeac3.jpg: **Called T cells look like small single cells with their transcripts inside the cell outline.** Close-ups of the two strongest T cells in each of the 12 sections (24 panels; title gives mouse, group, age, region and the cell's class / type label). Filled shapes are Xenium cell polygons coloured by cell class; the called T cell is outlined in red with its nucleus dashed, and dots are T-cell transcripts (red Cd3d/e/g / Cd247, blue Cd8a/b1, orange Cxcr6, purple Lck/Itk/Cd2, black Ptprc); scale bar 20 um. The called cells are compact, roughly round and carry dense clusters of T-cell transcripts within their own outline, which argues against smears from neighbours; many sit among endothelial cells along vessels and meninges, some among OLs.
figs/dddfffbf19270839.jpg: **T cells are scattered across every section, many at meninges, ventricles and vessels.** Whole-section maps of the 12 sections (cells faintly coloured by class) with each called T cell marked as a red circle; titles give mouse, group, age, the number of T cells and how many lie in border regions (meninges, ventricles, vasculature on the old region map). Counts range from 6 (RB4630, RB4653, both non-responders) to 33 (control RB4350), with no responder excess. RB4658 shows 0 border T cells although several sit at the section edge; that is a gap in its region map, not biology.
figs/2ca7acfb22111fde.jpg: **Responders do not have more T cells; two of them have more T cells sitting among OLs.** One dot per section (blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder, responders named). From left: T cells per 10k cells (p = 0.46), T cells away from borders per 10k cells (p = 0.29), fraction of T cells away from borders (p = 0.70), and fraction of T cells labelled as oligodendrocytes (p = 0.06); p values are exact permutation tests, responders vs controls. Non-responders have the fewest T cells. RB4627 and RB4405 have about 0.4 of their T cells labelled OL versus at most about 0.19 in controls, a lead to check with IHC rather than evidence of T-cell-driven damage; the control at 1.0 'away from borders' (RB4658) is a region-map artefact.
figs/7cf921b38f47a181.jpg: **No non-responder carries a hidden tail of highly stressed OLs.** Each OL is converted to its percentile among control OLs of the same slide and region (own section left out), which is uniform (flat at density 1) if a section looks like controls. A1/B1: histograms of these percentiles per section for the prespecified ISR score (A) and the data-derived up driver genes (B); blue = controls, dashed orange = non-responders, thick orange = responders. A2-A4 / B2-B4: one dot per section, observed / expected share of OLs above the control 90th, 99th and 99.9th percentile (log scale; filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder). Responders pile up in the top percentiles (ISR top 1 %: 5.0-8.3x), while all three non-responders stay inside the control range at every threshold.
figs/7b32053117dd56c7.jpg: **Non-responders have no regional pocket of stressed OLs; responders are elevated in every region.** Heatmaps of the observed / expected share of OLs above the control 99th percentile, per section (rows: 6 controls, 3 non-responders, 3 responders) and region (columns, old region map); left = prespecified ISR score, right = data-derived up driver genes. Numbers are the ratios, colour is log2 of the ratio (red = excess). Responders reach 2.3-11.5x for ISR and up to about 37x for drivers in every region, strongest in thalamus and fibre tracts, while the highest non-responder cells (RB4630 fibre tracts 1.6x ISR, RB4653 cortex 3.1x drivers) sit within the control range. Hippocampus has few OLs per section, so its ratios swing widely even in controls (0.0 to 4.5x).
figs/dc001bad14c7c5d0.jpg: **The ISR tail test would have caught a non-responder with as little as about 3 % responding OLs.** Spike-in simulation: a given percentage of a control section's OLs (x axis) is replaced with draws from a responding component estimated from responders, and the y axis gives the fraction of 120 trials (20 per control) where that section's tail enrichment exceeds every other control. Blue = prespecified ISR, orange = data-derived drivers; solid = top-1 % rule, dashed = top-10 % rule; the chance rate at 0 % is 1/6. The ISR top-1 % rule detects 3 % responding OLs in 0.98 of trials, whereas the driver score needs about 10-20 % because one control (RB4350) has a high driver tail.
figs/aa116f09d5d0366f.jpg: **In responders at least a fifth to a third of OLs respond; non-responders stay within control noise.** Nonparametric lower bound on the share of a section's OLs that come from a shifted (responding) distribution, computed from each section's percentiles against controls; one dot per section (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder, responders named). With the prespecified ISR score (left) responders reach 0.20-0.36 versus 0-0.07 in controls and 0-0.05 in non-responders; with the data-derived driver genes (right, circular for responders) responders reach 0.39-0.79. The response is all-or-none per mouse rather than a small responding subset in every animal.
figs/07c429712eed3999.jpg: **mtDSB responder OLs share an immune-visible core with EAE OLs but carry their own ISR and cell-cycle genes.** Each dot is a gene (2,967 genes above 20 CPM in mtDSB OLs): y = log2 fold change of mtDSB responder OLs vs same-slide controls (pseudobulk per mouse), x = log2 fold change in the EAE spinal-cord atlas for lesion OLs vs control OLs (A), normal-appearing OLs vs control OLs (B) or DAO vs MOL within EAE (C). Coloured dots are mtDSB driver genes by programme; grey are all other genes. Genome-wide correlation is weak (r = 0.29, 0.10, 0.18). ISR / cell-cycle genes (Trib3, Cdkn1a, Atf5, Sesn2, Ddit3, Nmu, Cd40) rise strongly only on the y axis, while Serpina3n, Cd74, H2-D1 and B2m rise in both, and interferon genes (Irf1, Psmb8, Gbp7) mainly in EAE.
figs/565d9e66f39ade55.jpg: **mtDSB OLs switch on the ISR and cell-cycle programmes, EAE OLs the interferon-gamma / MHC programmes, and both share an immune / reactive core.** Bars give the mean log2 fold change over each programme's genes (those above 20 CPM in mtDSB OLs) for four contrasts: mtDSB responders vs controls (orange), EAE lesion OLs vs control OLs (dark green), EAE normal-appearing OLs vs control OLs (light green) and DAO vs MOL within EAE (grey). ATF4 / ISR (about 1.8), cell cycle / survival (2.5) and prespecified ISR are high only in mtDSB; MHC class I, interferon type I and IFN-gamma are far higher in EAE lesions (about 1.3-3.3); immune / reactive is similar in both (about 2.3-2.4). Note: the 'ISR (prespecified, 10 genes)' bar uses only the 6 of 10 genes that pass the 20 CPM filter.
figs/fc6ff5c2b60dd2ad.jpg: **No EAE stage drives the OL ISR to mtDSB-responder levels, though the single top EAE mouse reaches the mildest responder.** A: per-mouse mean OL ISR score in the EAE spinal-cord atlas, z-scored against the atlas's own control (CFA) mouse x niche rows, by disease stage (x axis, from CFA controls through onset, peak and remission); light green = OLs in normal-appearing tissue, dark green = OLs in lesion niches, one dot per mouse x niche. B: the same score for the 12 mtDSB brains, z-scored against the 3 controls on the same slide (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder). EAE values stay between about -4 and +4 (top: 4.1 at PEAK1, normal-appearing), whereas responders sit at about 4.0, 6.4 and 8.9; the two z scales rest on different numbers of controls, so the comparison is approximate.
figs/0299b701acb0b122.jpg: **Pallidum is nearly absent from all three responder sections on the original region map.** Heatmap of the percentage of each section's cells assigned to each region (rows: 6 controls, 3 non-responders, 3 responders, with age; columns: regions from the original transcript-based map). Pallidum holds 0.0-0.7 % of cells in responders against 3.1-7.3 % in every control and non-responder, and fibre tracts are slightly larger in responders (8.6-10.8 %); other regions are comparable. This was first read as a section-plane difference; a later disease-free map (§43) showed that disease had distorted the region labels instead.
figs/c6e5db17cdd1f6f1.jpg: **Responders gain microglia in thalamus and fibre tracts; non-responders look like controls.** Heatmaps of log2(group mean density / control mean density) for 7 cell types (rows) in 6 regions (columns, original region map); left = responders vs controls, right = non-responders vs controls; * marks exact permutation p < 0.05 (3 vs 6 mice). Microglia rise +0.76 (thalamus) and +1.16 (fibre tracts) in responders, and OL density drops modestly in cortex and fibre tracts. The large neuronal ratios (e.g. 'Neurons' +1.88 in fibre tracts, excitatory neurons +2.45 in hypothalamus) come from small, noisy counts and region mislabelling, not real neuron gain; none of these tests survive FDR on their own.
figs/151620f5753ecb7a.jpg: **Per-mouse densities behind the microgliosis and the small OL loss.** Cells per mm2 for microglia (top row) and oligodendrocytes incl. DA-OLs (bottom row) in thalamus, fibre tracts, hypothalamus and cortex; one dot per section (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder), with exact permutation p for responders and non-responders vs controls in each title. Microglia in thalamus (92-153 vs 60-82 /mm2) and fibre tracts (71-219 vs 51-68) separate responders from controls (both p = 0.012), though RB4401 is close to controls in fibre tracts. OL density is lower in responder cortex and fibre tracts (p = 0.036) but overlaps the control range.
figs/9036143a17b3597b.jpg: **Without region labels, the microglia excess sits in OL-rich (white-matter-like) tissue, not grey matter.** Each section was cut into 100 um squares, squares were binned by their OL fraction (0-10 %, 10-30 %, 30-50 %, 50-100 %), and microglia per mm2 was computed per section per bin; one dot per section (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder), exact permutation p in each title. Responders have more microglia in 10-30 % (p = 0.024) and 30-50 % (p = 0.012) OL squares, a trend at 50-100 % (p = 0.083), and none in OL-poor squares (p = 0.75). The effect is graded across responders (RB4405 strongest, up to about 229 /mm2; RB4401 inside the control range in the purest white matter), and one non-responder (RB4403) is also high, attributed later to over-segmentation.
figs/27964be303767954.jpg: **Responders show a modest rise in proliferating microglia.** One dot per section (filled blue = control, open orange = non-responder, filled orange = responder), exact permutation p vs controls in each title. Left: percentage of microglia carrying at least one proliferation transcript (15-17 % in responders vs 11-15 % in controls, p = 0.012). Middle: observed / expected proliferating microglia, where expected comes from a model fitted on control microglia that accounts for sequencing depth and region (1.17-1.23 vs 0.87-1.14, p = 0.024). Right: proliferating microglia per mm2 of section (p = 0.012). A single transcript is a weak proliferation call, so this is supportive rather than conclusive.
figs/5532f2deb7643f64.jpg: **Microglia are not piled up around the most stressed OLs.** Left: for each section (one line), the mean number of microglia within 50 um of an OL, by the OL's ISR percentile band among same-slide, same-region controls, relative to OLs below the 50th percentile (= 1); blue thin = controls, thick orange = responders, dashed orange = non-responders. Right: the ratio for the top band (> 99th percentile) per section; responders (1.05-1.28) are not significantly above controls (0.90-1.15; p = 0.14) or non-responders (p = 0.60). The extra microglia of responders are spread through the affected tissue rather than recruited to individual stressed OLs, though a small focal component cannot be ruled out with 3 vs 6 mice.
figs/be04ab04aef37049.jpg: **Maps show the extra microglia concentrated in responder thalamus and surrounding white matter.** Whole-section maps of six sections (P60 control, two P60 responders, P21 control, P21 responder, P21 non-responder): microglia in red over OLs in light blue, other cells grey; the title gives whole-section microglia per mm2. RB4405 (132 /mm2) has a dense microglia patch in the thalamus, RB4627 and RB4401 show smaller thalamic accumulations, while controls and the non-responder look evenly spread. Whole-section density hides most of this (RB4401 98 vs control 94 /mm2); the maps are qualitative.
figs/3a0a487980805e96.jpg: **Segmentation spill-over: each cell type's pseudobulk carries a few percent of its neighbours' RNA.** Heatmap of the contamination fraction alpha, the median ratio of a source cell type's specific marker CPM in the target pseudobulk to that in the source itself, estimated in control mice (rows = target, columns = source; the diagonal is 1 by definition). Most off-diagonal values are 0.01-0.14, i.e. other cell types carry a few percent of OL, microglial and endothelial signal and somewhat more astrocytic signal. Neural stem cells carry 0.32 astrocyte signal and immature OL II / III 0.24 / 0.73 OL signal (partly genuine shared markers, so an upper bound); the neuron column rests on only 5 markers and is least reliable. These alphas feed the model that splits each responder change into a cell's own response and spill-over.
figs/83576cdea26808fa.jpg: **Genes that survive both the spill-over filter and the region check, by cell type.** Horizontal bars are responder-vs-control log2 fold changes (whole-section pseudobulk, pyDESeq2) for genes called own changes and reproduced in at least two regions; D3a shows rises, D3b falls, and bar colour marks the cell type named in brackets. Microglia carry the largest rises (Cst7, Lpl, Rab7b, Igf1, Axl, Csf1) with falls in homeostatic genes (P2ry12, P2ry13, Ccr1); astrocytes show reactive and type-I interferon genes (Cxcl10, Serpina3n, Isg15, Ifit1); OLs show the ISR and p53 arm (Trib3, Cdkn1a, Atf5, Sesn2). The large neuronal falls (Foxd2, Gsx1, Fgl1, Fzd5) are nucleus markers, read in the catalogue as section plane, and astrocyte Mbp is a likely leftover of spill-over.
figs/a6d1e1bf6e08e4df.jpg: **After the spill-over filter, microglia and NSCs keep almost all their hits, while most neuronal and immature-OL hits are neighbours' RNA.** Each bar is the number of genes changed in responders vs controls in one cell type (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 0.5), split into own changes (orange; the mixing model predicts < 50 % of the change from other cell types) and changes explained by spill-over (grey). Microglia have 135 own of 152 hits and neural stem cells 133 of 133; neurons keep only 12 of 38, and immature OL I/II/III hits are nearly all spill-over. The NSC hits are later shown to reflect section plane, not biology (run 39).
figs/39fd2d866cb50cae.jpg: **Interferon-positive astrocytes are not organised around microglia or stressed OLs.** Each point is one mouse: the within-section correlation r between an astrocyte being IFN-positive and (left) the number of microglia within 50 um or (right) the mean OL ISR score within 50 um, both centred within region and adjusted for local cell density; blue = controls, open orange = non-responders, filled orange = responders. All r values lie within about +/-0.03, i.e. no meaningful coupling in any mouse. The responder-vs-control difference is p = 0.024 for microglia (carried by one responder at r ~ 0.03) and p = 0.26 for OL ISR.
figs/44e0b55f177d799f.jpg: **More astrocytes carry type-I interferon transcripts in responder thalamus and fibre tracts, but the rise is small and not responder-specific.** Each point is one mouse: the percentage of astrocytes with at least one IFN-I gene-set transcript in a region (six panels); blue = controls, open orange = non-responders, filled orange = responders, with exact permutation p-values in the panel titles. Responders rise in thalamus and fibre tracts (both p = 0.012), not in hypothalamus, cortex, striatum or hippocampus. One non-responder has the highest fibre-tract value of all (about 23 %), so region-level IFN-positivity does not track the OL response.
figs/af2be848606b8756.jpg: **The NSC 'response' reflects which ventricle wall is in the section, not more proliferation.** Each point is one mouse (circles P21, squares P60; blue controls, open orange non-responders, filled orange responders). Left: % of NSCs that are Tbx3+ (third-ventricle/tanycyte); middle: % of NSCs with any proliferation transcript; right: % proliferating among Foxg1+ (lateral-ventricle) NSCs. P60 controls have 11-14 % Tbx3+ NSCs and P60 responders almost none, while proliferation does not differ overall (p = 0.45) or within the same niche (p = 0.38).
figs/ecb1bf89d50ed1a0.jpg: **Inside OLs the response is ATF4/ISR plus p53; mitophagy and cGAS-STING barely move.** O1a: each point is one mouse's pathway score, the mean log2 fold change of the set's genes in OL + DA-OL whole-section pseudobulk vs same-slide controls (blue controls, open orange non-responders, filled orange responders), for 11 prespecified pathways. O1b: per-gene responder-vs-control log2FC grouped by pathway; grey bars are genes whose change is >= 50 % explained by spill-over, and * marks genes below 5 CPM in control OLs. ATF4/ISR (about +1.9) and p53 targets (about +1.0) separate cleanly from controls; the small cGAS-STING/IFN-I rise comes mostly from grey (spill-over) interferon-stimulated genes, while the sensors themselves stay flat.
figs/6bd68939208d9bcf.jpg: **OPCs rise no more than astrocytes; the ISR response is confined to mature, myelinating OLs.** Each point is one mouse: ISR transcripts (Trib3, Atf5, Ddit3, Gdf15, Sesn2, Cebpg, Cdkn1a) per 1,000 counts per cell, averaged per mouse and divided by the control mean, in OPCs (Pdgfra+ Mog-), astrocytes (taken as the spill-over level) and mature OLs including DA-OLs; blue controls, open orange non-responders, filled orange responders. Responder mature OLs reach about 3-5x the control level, while OPCs and astrocytes both sit at about 1.1-1.35x. One non-responder's OPCs (about 1.22x) sit above two responders.
figs/0b574c0ee08c9d28.jpg: **Counting every transcript, inside and outside cells, late myelin genes fall in every region while Sox10 does not.** Heat maps of log2 (responders / controls) for 13 genes (columns) in five regions (rows), computed from raw Xenium transcripts binned on a 20 um grid without using cell outlines; left per mm2 of region, right per OL in the region; * marks p < 0.05 (exact permutation, mouse as unit). Mog, Opalin and Cldn11 fall by about 0.7-1.1 log2 per OL in all regions, Sox10 stays near 0, and Trib3, Cdkn1a and Gfap rise strongly. Snap25 (neuronal negative control) is flat per mm2; its per-OL rise in cortex reflects the smaller OL denominator.
figs/e57535a981f634ba.jpg: **Per-mouse myelin and lineage transcripts per OL in fibre tracts and cortex.** Each point is one mouse: transcripts of Mog, Opalin, Mbp and Sox10 per OL (segmentation-free counts) in fibre tracts (top) and cortex (bottom); blue controls, open orange non-responders, filled orange responders, with permutation p-values in the titles. Mog per OL is lower in all three responders in both regions (p = 0.012), Opalin falls as well (p = 0.024 fibre tracts, 0.060 cortex), Mbp is weaker (one responder within the control range), and Sox10 does not change (p = 0.89 and 1.0). Non-responders sit with controls throughout.
figs/0702f26a13e05162.jpg: **With the disease-free region map, pallidum reappears in responders and fibre tracts shrink to control size.** Each point is one section/mouse: % of the section's cells labelled pallidum (left) or fibre tracts (middle) on the original map (circles) and the disease-free map from 400 anatomy genes (squares), lines joining the same mouse; right, % of each section's cells whose new label agrees with the original. Responder pallidum rises from about 0-0.7 % to 1.8-3.9 % (p 0.012 -> 0.31) and responder fibre tracts fall from 8.6-10.8 % to 5.4-7.7 % (p 0.012 -> ~0.6), into the control range. Agreement with the original labels is about 92-95 % in controls, lower in responders (about 90-94 %) and lowest in one non-responder (about 86 %).
figs/8a35776c6da1455a.jpg: **Region maps before and after re-labelling: the disease had turned responder pallidum into 'fibre tract'.** Each panel is one coronal section with every cell coloured by region (legend at bottom), oriented dorsal up and midline right; top row original labels, bottom row labels re-drawn from disease-free anatomy genes, with pallidum and fibre-tract shares printed above each section. Six sections are shown: a P60 control, two P60 responders, a P21 control, a P21 responder and a P21 non-responder. In responders (e.g. RB4405: pallidum 0.0 % -> 3.9 %, fibre tracts 10.8 % -> 5.4 %) the black fibre-tract area beside the internal capsule turns back into magenta pallidum, while control and non-responder maps barely change.
figs/64eee63a4ee97637.jpg: **Regional results on both maps: OL stress ranking holds with pallidum joining the top, and thalamus microgliosis holds.** For each region, bars show the control range (min-max; light = original map, dark = disease-free map) and orange markers the three responders (circles original map, squares disease-free map); * marks responders vs controls p < 0.05 (exact permutation). Left: share of OLs above the same-slide control 90th ISR percentile; right: microglia per mm2. On the disease-free map OL stress is raised in all regions except olfactory areas, with thalamus, fibre tracts and pallidum highest; microglia density stays significant in thalamus and fibre tracts and becomes significant in hypothalamus, while the original map's 'too few microglia in responder pallidum' disappears.
figs/3811e74dfb0c950d.jpg: **The three responders share a response in microglia and in OL genes that were never used to call them.** Each point is one mouse: Pearson r over genes between its pseudobulk profile (log2 expression minus same-slide controls) and the mean profile of the other responders, per cell type; OL profiles exclude every selection gene (ISR, driver, ATF4/ISR and p53 sets). Blue controls form the null, open orange are non-responders, filled orange responders. Microglia separate completely (responders about 0.57-0.82 vs controls up to about 0.42, p = 0.012) and OLs without selection genes nearly so (p = 0.036, one responder level with the top control); astrocytes (p = 0.24) and endothelial cells (p = 0.14) do not separate.
figs/c45e7233e48df176.jpg: **Most key per-mouse claims hold with any one responder left out.** Heat map of 17 per-mouse metrics (rows) for all 12 mice (columns: six controls, three non-responders, three responders, with age), each value a z-score against same-slide controls using the pooled control SD; row labels give the 3-vs-6 exact p and the worst p with one responder dropped. The OL ISR score, ATF4/ISR and p53 scores, microglial DAM, astrocyte reactivity, thalamus microglia density and Mog per OL are extreme in all three responders, while non-responders resemble controls. Weaker rows are carried by two responders: OL held-out r and Mbp per OL (RB4401 near controls) and hypothalamus microglia density; the expected-null Sox10 per OL is flat (p = 0.89), and RB4403's high label-free microglia density (z = 4.1) is attributed to over-segmentation.
figs/576c0e9e26c622c5.jpg: **Region x age DE on the disease-free map largely reproduces the original run, except in pallidum.** R3a: Pearson r of mtDSB-vs-control log2 fold changes over shared genes between the original and the disease-free region labels, per cell type (rows) and region (columns); 'nan' where a pseudobulk was not available. R3b: each point is one cell type x region x age, significant genes with original (x) vs disease-free (y) labels, with the identity line. Fold changes agree closely (r about 0.8-0.99) in thalamus, hypothalamus, striatum and cortex, are somewhat lower in fibre tracts and drop to about 0.6 in pallidum, the region the original map had mislabelled; hit counts sit near the diagonal.
figs/477276fad19709f2.jpg: **In MS lesion OLs, the mtDSB core set rises modestly while the interferon-gamma and immune-OL sets rise as much or more.** Heat map of gene-set scores (mean log2FC of set genes in lesion OL pseudobulks vs that atlas's control samples) for 8 sets (rows) across lesion types in four public snRNA atlases (columns: Jäkel, Schirmer, Absinta, Lerma-Martin); * marks sample-level exact p < 0.05. MTDSB_CORE reaches about +0.8 to +1.2 in Schirmer, Absinta and Lerma-Martin, but IFNG reaches +1.3 to +2.8 and IMMUNE_OL up to +2.2, which is the EAE-like pattern; myelin sets barely move. Jäkel is inconsistent, with core and ISR falling in CA and CI lesions.
figs/4e746ea179bb4aac.jpg: **Gene by gene, the mtDSB-specific markers stay flat in MS OLs, while shared CHOP / p21 stress genes rise.** Heat map of log2FC vs controls for 16 genes (columns) in mouse references (top two rows: mtDSB responder OLs and EAE lesion OLs) and in MS lesion types from four snRNA atlases (rows below); dashed lines separate mtDSB-specific markers (TRIB3, GDF15, ATF5, EIF4EBP1), shared ISR / p53 stress genes, and inflammation genes; blank cells are genes missing from that reference. Mouse responders raise TRIB3 (+5.4), GDF15 (+4.3) and EIF4EBP1 (+3.0), whereas Absinta and Lerma-Martin lesions keep them within about -0.8 to +0.3 (only Schirmer rises, about +0.8 to +1.3). DDIT3 (CHOP), CDKN1A (p21) and SESN2 rise in most lesions, as do IRF1 and PSMB8 as in EAE.
figs/074c0068ba7859ad.jpg: **OLs carrying mtDSB-specific transcripts are rare in all MS atlases; DDIT3 + CDKN1A co-expressing OLs are more common in lesions.** Each point is one sample (blue control, orange lesion), per atlas (columns) and lesion type (x-axis). Top: % of OL nuclei with >= 2 summed transcripts of TRIB3, GDF15, ATF5 and EIF4EBP1; bottom: % of OL nuclei with both DDIT3 and CDKN1A. Specific-positive OLs are at or below about 0.5 % in Jäkel, Absinta and Lerma-Martin and not higher than controls; only Schirmer (deepest libraries) reaches a few percent, with CI lesion samples highest. CHOP + p21 OLs are near 0 % in controls and rise in some lesion samples (up to about 2-3 %). No statistical tests were run on these fractions.
figs/0b85e2d8b73af204.jpg: **Genome-wide, MS lesion OL changes correlate only weakly with either mouse model.** Each bar is the Pearson r over genes (about 2,100-2,400 shared genes) between the mean OL log2FC of one MS lesion type and a mouse OL profile: mtDSB responders (orange), EAE lesion (blue) or EAE DAO vs MOL state (grey). All correlations are below about 0.17 in absolute value except Schirmer CI vs the EAE DAO state (about -0.34). In Schirmer, Absinta and Lerma-Martin, r with mtDSB exceeds r with EAE lesion in every lesion type, while Jäkel leans the other way; there is no null or confidence interval.
figs/6bb5312b5af37ed8.jpg: **Myelin RNA defines lesion zones in the four human Xenium sections.** Top: every cell coloured by local myelin RNA (MOG + MBP + MAG + CNP + MOBP counts per 1,000 counts among all cells within 100 um; dark = low, bright = high). Bottom: the resulting zones per cell: demyelinated (red, < 25 % of the section's myelinated level), edge (orange, < 60 %), myelinated (blue) and neuron-rich grey matter (grey, excluded). In the two MS sections (MS-1, MS-2; spinal cord / brainstem-like cross-sections) the demyelinated zone runs largely along the tissue border with patches inside, whereas the two Baló sections are mostly grey matter with little white matter. Panel titles show the MS sections by case number (MS-1 and MS-2 here); there is no pathology annotation or control tissue.
figs/e5bc8ebf26aadd1d.jpg: **Lesion OLs raise TRIB3, EIF4EBP1, p21 and PUMA and lose MOG / OPALIN while SOX10 stays flat; neighbouring cells change these genes much less.** Heat maps of log2 expression (pooled per zone, per 10,000 counts) in edge or demyelinated zones vs the myelinated zone of the same section, for OLs (left) and for all other cells as a spill-over control (right); columns are MS-1 and MS-2 edge and demyelinated zones and the Baló-2 edge zone (column labels show the MS sections by case number), and rows are grouped into mtDSB markers, p53 / stress, inflammation, hypoxia and lineage / myelin genes. In demyelinated MS-1 / MS-2 zones OLs show TRIB3 +1.3 / +1.4, CDKN1A +1.8 / +2.3, BBC3 +1.7 / +2.4, MOG -2.3 / -2.6 and SOX10 near 0; other cells change TRIB3, CDKN1A and BBC3 by at most about 0.4. GDF15 also rises strongly in other cells (+2.8 / +1.9), so the OL GDF15 signal may partly be neighbours' RNA, and MOG / OPALIN fall in other cells too.
figs/49883adaa21f3f04.jpg: **Near the tissue border even myelinated OLs carry stress transcripts; deep in the tissue, demyelinated OLs still exceed myelinated ones.** Each point is the % of OLs carrying a transcript (TRIB3, CDKN1A, BBC3, or the combined TRIB3/EIF4EBP1 + CDKN1A/BBC3 event) in one zone (blue myelinated, orange edge, red demyelinated) and one distance-from-border bin (< 150, 150-400, > 400 um), circles MS-1 and squares MS-2 (titles show case numbers). In MS-1, myelinated OLs within 400 um of the border carry CDKN1A in about 13.5-15 %, versus about 4 % deeper. In the > 400 um bin, demyelinated OLs (red) lie above myelinated ones (blue) for every marker in both sections, which is why later ratios are restricted to deep OLs.
figs/4e5411e4fc9e99c6.jpg: **Demyelinated-zone OLs carry stress transcripts several times more often than myelinated-zone OLs; other cells mostly do not.** Each point is a rate ratio (share of cells with >= 1 transcript in the demyelinated zone / share in the myelinated zone of the same section, log scale) with a 95 % spatial block-bootstrap CI (250 um blocks, 300 resamples), for OLs (orange) and other cells (grey) in MS-1, MS-2 (labelled by case number) and the two Baló sections, per marker (panels). In both MS sections OLs show about 2.8-3.5x for TRIB3, about 2.8x for CDKN1A, 3.4-4.8x for BBC3 and 3-5x for the combined event, with CIs above 1, while other cells stay near 1 for TRIB3, CDKN1A and BBC3. GDF15 rises in both OLs and other cells; the Baló sections show only other cells, because too few OLs fall in their demyelinated zones.
figs/171b2f8db34f78f7.jpg: **Away from the tissue border, the share of stressed OLs rises as local myelin RNA falls.** For white-matter OLs more than 400 um from the border, binned by local myelin RNA relative to the section's myelinated level (x-axis, < 0.15 to > 1), each line shows the % of OLs carrying TRIB3, CDKN1A, BBC3 or the combined event (panels), per section (MS-1 and MS-2 labelled by case number, Baló-2; Baló-1 has no bin with >= 50 OLs). In both MS sections all markers are highest at low myelin RNA and lowest above the myelinated level (for example CDKN1A falls from about 10-14 % to about 2-3 %), though the trend is not strictly monotonic in the lowest bins. This is descriptive only: no trend test or per-bin CI, and myelin RNA partly comes from the OLs themselves.
figs/e9d92fa8272715f0.jpg: **OLs with the mtDSB-like signature sit mainly in and around the demyelinated rim.** Each panel is one MS section (MS-1 left, MS-2 right; titles show case numbers) with cells coloured by zone as in the zone maps (red demyelinated, orange edge, blue myelinated, grey grey matter) and black dots marking OLs that carry both arms (TRIB3 or EIF4EBP1 plus CDKN1A or BBC3). The black dots cluster in the red rim and adjacent orange edge zone near the tissue border, with fewer scattered through the myelinated interior. The maps include cells near the border, where stress transcripts are confounded (run 54).
